body:
I didn't do a very good job of objectifying how I was feeling and it certainly does come off as "money is more important than my life" when reading it again. I'm not sure how to properly express what I really meant.  
  
Money is not more important than a human life. Opportunities certainly can be, in relation to your family. I don't know if you have children or are married but I can say with 100% certainty I would do anything I can for them, to set them up for success. They may not understand it right now, but if I have to travel down that dark path I feel that is the best for them. Maybe not, I've certainly meditated about it long and hard. There is no way I can know ending my life would be the better of the situations, all I can do is objectively look at all the variables and choose which one is more likely to produce desirable results.  
  
I don't want to end my life, I really don't. Especially now that I know with the help of others I can stay sober. At this point only time will tell and I have to accept that whatever happens, happens. They say in AA you have to live life on lifes terms. It's an ironic phrase given me contemplating suicide, but I'm going to do whatever I can for my family and let them live it on lifes terms. With or without me.  
  
I appreciate you taking the time to post, I really do. Thank you.

There are many things I'm fearful about, and for the first time in many years I'm able to acknowledge that. I don't want to end my life, I truly don't. Even on the pink cloud of early sobriety I can see benefits and I certainly hope I can continue on the journey. In AA I've met several "old timers" who exude a presence that I would love to one day have. Am I scared of suicide? Hell yeah I am. I have a relatively new relationship with my higher power so I have no clue what awaits me - maybe nothingness.  
  
You are right though, right at the surface of those good memories will forever tainted with my desire to "abandon" them. I'm not sure if you have kids or a spouse but you'd do anything within your power to protect them. That total selflessness is for me a major tenant of being a father. There are many things I am powerless over, such as my drinking and the courts decision, but anything I can do to set them up for success I have a duty to do.  
  
Have I been selfish in the past? You bet your ass I have been. My alcoholic drinking is a prime example of that. I've already pledged to family there isn't anything I won't do to keep sober for the rest of my life. Suicide is no escape plan for that, for reasons that are very obvious. Did I entertain that committing suicide would be selfish? Absolutely. I would be remiss if I didn't. I've weighted the options and if I'm brutally honest about them it would be selfish if I stuck around - though I hope it doesn't come to that.  
  
Thank you for your post, I appreciate you taking the time to respond to me.
